items.note: Presentation featured three inscriptions and a separate focus on water bodies; stepwell photos recalled the Rani ki Vav of Patan.
items.gloss: We brought an exclusive section of three inscriptions to understand Udaipur's centuries-old journey on a timeline. We focused on the water bodies separately. Pictures of the splendid stepwells reminded one of Patan's Rani ki Vav in Gujarat.

items.note: Author: a hill at Udaypur was to be cut into a rock temple like Ellora but the work stopped early; he conjectures a king wanted to outdo Udayaditya, as Naravarman did with Vijay Mandir.
items.gloss: Go up the hill and you will find that, like the Ellora rock temple, a rock temple was to be made by cutting the hill at Udaipur. But the work stopped at an early stage. A few proofs remain today. Whichever king began it, I think he wanted to outdo his predecessor Udayaditya, just like King Naravarman who built Vijay Mandir in Vidisha trying to go several steps beyond his father's great construction at Udaipur. Perhaps he was about to create something even beyond Naravarman's Vijay temple.

items.note: Author conjectures the hilltop rock temple was an ambitious Paramara project that may have drawn craftsmen even from Ellora (conjecture, no source cited).
items.gloss: This rock temple visible from afar on a high hill must have been a very ambitious project of the Paramara dynasty. It is possible that craft and art experts as far as Ellora were summoned here. By then the rock temple at Ellora was complete and its fame had gone to craft experts. Who knows which Paramara representative called Ellora's skilled craftsmen and architects to Udaipur. Something like this must have happened.

items.note: Paramara kings also expressed devotion in hill-top architecture at Omkareshwar and Mandhata on the Narmada; hill monuments of faith at Chanderi and Gwalior.
items.gloss: Speaking of hilltop heights, at Omkareshwar and Mandhata too the Paramara kings expressed their devotion in sculpture on the Narmada's banks. At Chanderi and Gwalior also monuments of faith were built on hills.

items.note: Vijay Mandir at Vidisha, a hundred years after Naravarman, was destroyed by Iltutmish's attacks on Malwa and a mosque was made from its rubble.
items.gloss: A hundred years after King Naravarman it was looted and ruined by the merciless Turk raiders who had seized Delhi. That notorious invader was Iltutmish, in whose fierce attacks on Malwa it was broken. A mosque was made from the rubble of that huge temple.

items.note: Author: Udaypur's rock temple was meant to surpass the Vijay temple and its fragments but the project did not go far.
items.gloss: Even those broken pieces make the surviving glory of Udaipur look faded. Udaipur's rock temple was to outdo both of these, but this project could not go much further.

items.note: Author thinks the stalled work likely belongs to the later Paramara period, and that this was all that Paramara effort at Udaypur was fated to accomplish (conjecture).
items.gloss: It is quite possible this is an episode of the late Paramara period. Whatever had risen stopped there. In Udaipur's fate the Paramaras' work was written only this much.

items.note: Old Bhopal described as a vastu-planned square town with a Paramara-time Sabha Mandal temple-school; the Sabha Mandal was built after Bhoja by Udayaditya.
items.gloss: It was an orderly city settled in a square design under the rules of vastu, with today's Chowk Bazaar probably at its centre. In Paramara times this was the Sabha Mandal, the city's important Brahmasthana. It was a vast temple complex that was also a Sanskrit school, on the lines of the great Sarasvati Kanthabharanas of Ujjain, Dhar and Mandu. But the Sabha Mandal was built after Bhoja and was made by Udayaditya himself.

claim.value: built Sabha Mandal at Bhopal after Bhoja

items.note: Author states there is considerable evidence Bhoja founded Bhopal; the Bada Talab lies on his man-made dam.
items.gloss: There is considerable evidence that Bhopal was settled by Raja Bhoj. The Bada Talab still spreads over 36 square kilometres on the man-made dam built by him.

items.note: Author's remark on the crispness of the inscriptions: 'as if the stones had been taken out of a printer'.
items.gloss: Look at the inscriptions, as if the stones had been taken out of a printer. How skilled they must have been!

items.note: A ground report: illegal quarries run on over 2,500 hectares of forest land, lakhs of rupees of stone daily, local villagers hired at subsistence wages.
items.gloss: A ground report by Govind Saxena said illegal mines are running on more than two and a half thousand hectares of forest department land, from which stone worth lakhs of rupees is extracted every day. People of local villages are put to labour at wages barely enough to live. The wealthy stone looters blast the mines ruthlessly.

items.note: INTACH team's survey list: thousand-year-old tanks and stepwells, Nataraja Shiva on a 27-foot rock at Ravan Tol, Pisanhari temple, hill fortification, Bijamandal, a Jain residence, old gates, Bada Bazaar and palace ruins; found large-scale conservation urgently needed.
items.gloss: His team viewed from every corner the thousand-year-old tanks and stepwells, Nataraj Shiva on a 27-foot rock at Ravan Tol, the Pisanhari temple, the hill's fortification, Bijamandal, Malukdas Jain's residence, old gates, the Bada Bazaar and most importantly the palace ruins. They found Udaipur a place that really needed immediate large-scale conservation.

items.note: Author's belief that INTACH's visit was the first such notice of Udaypur since the Scindia State archaeology officer Garde about 150 years earlier.
items.gloss: I think that for the first time at this level someone had come to take notice of Udaipur, about one and a half hundred years after Garde Sahib, the archaeology officer of Scindia State of Gwalior.

items.note: INTACH team drew a field work plan and camped in Udaypur; four technically skilled members arrived and the administration was informed.
items.gloss: Returning to Bhopal the INTACH team made a field work plan. Within three days came the message that the team would camp in Udaipur until the work was done. Four technically skilled members had left for Udaipur. The administration was told about their work and the need for local revenue officers. As soon as they camped in Udaipur the team set to work.

items.note: Locals saw the effort as the start of development bringing outsiders and business.
items.gloss: Everyone we met had a curiosity awakening. They saw it as the start of the kind of development when outsiders would come more often. Their business would shine. In short it was about their own benefit.

items.gloss: The idol that had disappeared from that place he had brought back from somewhere four days earlier. They had come to show the INTACH team how heritage lies orphaned. They arrived full of enthusiasm but Uma-Maheshwar were not to be seen there.

items.note: Earlier visitors, like other tourists, went only to the temple; this visit invited walking the lanes.
items.gloss: Last time, like other tourists, they had returned from the temple alone. This time Udaipur's invitation was to roam its lanes.

items.note: Google Maps shows overgrown spots beside present houses where stone structures peeping out suggest old settlements, buildings and commercial complexes.
items.gloss: Udaipur's settlement must have had old-period colonies, buildings and trading complexes. With Google Map many places beside or behind present houses were clearly visible, lost in untended greenery. Stone structures peeping from them hint that some structures must have been there.

items.note: Behind Bijamandal, stone buildings' back walls show the arrangement of stones from several different periods.
items.gloss: We went into the dense bushes in front of Bijamandal and made our way to stone buildings, which were the back walls of buildings that must open elsewhere in front. The arrangement of stones behind them clearly showed the story of several different periods.

items.note: Stones at the back of a Ram temple are the oldest; shops of the old Bada Bazaar were probably built later, all more than five hundred years old.
items.gloss: The stones at the back of a Ram temple were the oldest, near which the old shop buildings of the big market were probably raised later. But all these too must be more than five hundred years old.

items.note: Proposal that the heritage team clean the overgrowth weekly, as a local phase of a cleanliness campaign, rather than leave it all to government.
items.gloss: I suggested that every week Udaipur's heritage team take up cleaning these thickets. If we only clean these tangles, Udaipur's clear face can emerge. We should not leave everything to the government. A local phase of the Swachhta Abhiyan could begin here, in which rubbish will not be cleaned but centuries of settled dust removed.

items.note: A small temple finely carved, standing on a seven-foot platform in a corner of a large debris-and-bush-covered complex; platform sinking into ground.
items.gloss: It was carved so beautifully that it looked like metalwork cast in a factory from a computer design. Up a narrow lane in front of the temple, in a corner of a vast complex surrounded by debris and bushes, the temple stood on a seven-foot-high platform.
